observation_summary: The ExtendedMessageFormat class enters an infinite loop when parsing a pattern containing single quotes, leading to an OutOfMemoryError.
hypothesis: The method appendQuotedString fails to advance the ParsePosition when it encounters an escaped quote, causing the loop in applyPattern to repeatedly process the same character.
prediction: Adding a call to next(pos) before returning in the appendQuotedString method will correctly advance the parser and prevent the infinite loop.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly identifies that the fix requires advancing the parse position (next(pos)) when an escaped quote is detected, confirming the root cause is an incorrect algorithmic step in the parsing logic.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an infinite loop caused by a failure to update the parser's state (the ParsePosition) during a specific branch of the parsing algorithm. This is a classic procedural logic error where the iteration strategy is flawed, fitting the Algorithm/Method category perfectly.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves a condition, the primary issue is not a missing guard but a failure to update the algorithm's state (the parse position) within the existing logic.
The issue is not about an incorrect value or initialization, but about the procedural flow of the parsing algorithm.
